cards.explanation: The answer is breaking faith, friends. Malachi asks, "Why then do we break faith with one another so as to profane the covenant of our fathers?" (Malachi 2:10). He says "we," so he counts himself in. The question is plain: same Father, same God, so why treat each other like that?

The answer is by marrying the daughter of a foreign god, friends. The text says Judah profaned the LORD's beloved sanctuary "…by marrying the daughter of a foreign god." (Malachi 2:11). Malachi calls it an abomination and says it happened in Israel and in Jerusalem. That's how seriously he says it.

The answer is False, friends. Malachi says, "…may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob everyone who is awake and aware…" and he says it even if the man brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts (Malachi 2:12). So the man is not safe. The offering doesn't change that.

The answer is that the LORD no longer receives their offerings gladly, bakers. Malachi says they cover the altar with tears "…because He no longer regards your offerings or receives them gladly from your hands." (Malachi 2:13). The weeping is real. The text gives that reason and no other.

The answer is True, friends. The people ask "Why?" and Malachi answers, "It is because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth…" (Malachi 2:14). The LORD is the witness between a man and his wife. I think that's a heavy thing to hear, and Malachi says it straight.

The answer is companion, friends. Malachi says she is "…your companion and your wife by covenant." (Malachi 2:14). A companion is someone who walks beside you. She's named that way right alongside the covenant.
The answer is godly, bakers. Malachi asks, "And why one?" and answers, "Because He seeks godly offspring." (Malachi 2:15). That's the reason the text gives. Short answer, big meaning.

The answer is True, friends. Malachi says, "So guard yourselves in your spirit and do not break faith with the wife of your youth." (Malachi 2:15). It's a plain instruction. Guard your spirit and keep your word to her.
The answer is divorce, bakers. The LORD, the God of Israel, says, "For I hate divorce…" (Malachi 2:16). He says it in His own words. I think it's worth slowing down on that one.
